author: original (NevaIB)
title: Indefinite integrals and reverse chain rule

points.text: Antiderivatives of x^n, sin x, cos x, 1/x and e^x
Composites with a linear inner function ax+b
Integration by inspection or substitution for k g'(x) f(g(x))

bigPicture: Every derivative in 5.6 gives an integral when read backwards. With a linear inner function, divide by its coefficient; with g′(x) in front of f(g(x)), integrate by inspection.

keyIdeas.answer: x^n → x^(n+1)/(n + 1) (n ≠ −1); 1/x → ln|x|; sin x → −cos x; cos x → sin x; e^x → e^x; always + C.

keyIdeas.cue: Composites with a linear inner function ax + b?
keyIdeas.answer: ∫f(ax + b) dx = (1/a)F(ax + b) + C. Examples: ∫cos 3x dx = (1/3) sin 3x + C; ∫1/(2x + 1) dx = ½ ln|2x + 1| + C.
If the integrand is k g′(x) f(g(x)), the answer is k F(g(x)) + C. Example: ∫2x(x² + 1)⁴ dx = (x² + 1)⁵/5 + C. Substitution u = g(x) gives the same result.

keyTerms.def: recognising the integrand as a derivative from the chain rule
replacing g(x) with u to simplify an integral

solution: (b) derivative of x² + 4 is 2x, so ½ ln(x² + 4)
practice.answer: (a) ½e^(2x) − ⅓cos 3x + C (b) ½ ln(x² + 4) + C

Expanding instead of spotting the pattern (works, but slow)
